main_text.p: cortice obtinent vim calefaciendi scilicet discutiendi & exiccandi. Ad extremum de liquore acido sciendum, cum saccharo coqui, seruariq; ad aestatis aestuantis febres, pestilentiæq; contagia certo experimento. Ipsa vero poma in Magnatum aulisin taleo-las conciduntur, sacchariq; polline aspersa manducantur prima mensa, acetariorum vi-cem supplentia; sed ita comesa difficulter in ventriculo confici extra dubium est, prædu-ra enim caro est, pituitosa ac gelida, unde colicos excitari dolores necesse est, si immodi-cè & frequentius efitetur[?].
main_text.head: Submonitio ad locum de citriis, &c.
main_text.p: Graeci & Arabes in qualitatibus citrii mali recensendis nequaquam conueniunt. Auicenna corticem citri calidum esse ait, in primo, & siccum in gradu secundo. Galenus siccum absolute in secundo, nec calidum contra asseruit[?]. Idem Auicenna carnem dicit calidam, Galenus & Æginetæ frigidam. Semen decoctum suauem ori conciliare odorem, corpusq; reddere pingue scribit, quorum postremum a nullo Græcorum traditum est, omnemq; excedit rationem. Acidam ciusparem[?] bonum esse nutrimentum gutturi[?] & pulmoni contendit, quoniam utrumq; rationi, alierum[?] Serapioni etiam

page.notes: The first word of the initial paragraph is a large woodcut initial G, read as "Graeci" with [?]. Italic and roman boundaries in the lower paragraph are uncertain. Doubtful readings: "efitetur", "asseruit", "ciusparem", "gutturi", "alierum", and the page number. The running head and page number are read from the scan. The catchword "contra-" is at the lower right.
